thesis: The AI buildout's binding constraint has moved from chips to concrete: power, water, and local consent now decide who can build.
why_now: OpenAI is now negotiating grid reliability directly with utilities, data-center water startups are consolidating, and voters are rejecting new data centers — while Oracle raises $20B and Nebius plans $40B of spending into the same constrained system.
evidence: Omen AI adds liquid know-how in $16 million Aquatic Labs acquisition
Voters reject AI data centers, Shield AI’s $5.3B Echodyne deal, and a Seattle startup’s rare double exit
angle: Build the boring plumbing of the buildout: grid-interconnection tooling, water-recycling and cooling retrofits, and community-impact analytics that turn a data-center proposal from a fight into a permit.

thesis: The next AI moat is being soldered, not trained: optical interconnect is where incumbents are spending $115B and startups are sneaking in at the chiplet level.
why_now: Marvell's $115B Lumentum acquisition prices optical components as strategic infrastructure, while a $4.6M seed-stage chiplet-interconnect startup and a $720M inference-chip raise show the stack is still open at the edges.
evidence: Marvell to acquire optical component maker Lumentum in massive $115B deal
Staera launches with $4.6M to develop an optical interconnect for chiplets
British inference chip developer Fractile raises $720M in funding
angle: Attack the seams the giants can't cover: chiplet-to-chiplet optical I/O, co-packaged optics tooling, or interconnect test and validation — sell to the neoclouds who need bandwidth without buying the whole Marvell catalog.

thesis: Agents are getting cheap to demo and ruinous to run — the winners this cycle will be the companies that meter, distill, and cap agent spend.
why_now: LangChain just hit a $3B valuation on agent management and Fal doubled to $16B on inference demand, while AWS is shipping per-user cost attribution for Bedrock — the market is now pricing the agent bill, not just the agent demo.
evidence: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges
Cost attribution and controls for AI developer and productivity tools on Amazon Bedrock
angle: Build the FinOps layer for agents: per-task cost accounting, automatic model downgrading and distillation of hot paths, and hard spend caps with approval flows — the control plane every enterprise agent deployment will be forced to buy.
